implementation.uapi: Added struct agi_lc_event_backpressure, explicit NORMAL/NEAR_FULL/FULL/LOSS states, and additive AGI_LC_EVENT_BACKPRESSURE ioctl 0x6c without changing the existing ABI number or single-entry/batch accounting interfaces.
implementation.reported_telemetry: The query reports ring capacity, queued records, cumulative dropped records, oldest and newest queued sequence, next sequence, and a sticky loss state when telemetry has been dropped.
implementation.security: The query requires a live non-revoked session and matching lifecycle lineage, validates all input/output fields, reads queue state under queue_lock, and copies results back only after unlocking.
implementation.productivity_impact: User-space runtimes can observe backpressure before issuing additional work, drain adaptively, reduce batch size, or escalate telemetry-loss handling. This is an adaptive-control primitive; it does not claim universal raw throughput improvement by itself.
implementation.selftest: Tenant QEMU fills the 64-entry ring, verifies the 65th accelerator event reports telemetry loss, queries backpressure, and asserts queued=64, capacity=64, dropped_records>0, LOSS state, and ordered sequence watermarks.

release_gate.reason: M156 is bounded QEMU/software validation. Operator-controlled signing, stable/LTS forward-port qualification, independent build-farm qualification, physical accelerator qualification, and external security governance remain required.
release_gate.hardware_claim: No physical GPU, NPU, VRAM, IOMMU, DMA, vendor-driver, reset, or fleet qualification is claimed.

known_limitations: Backpressure telemetry is advisory state for adaptive user-space control; the kernel does not automatically change batch size or drain user-space queues.
The LOSS state is sticky for the session through cumulative dropped_records and requires higher-level resynchronization policy.
The benchmark in the same gate is inherited M155 synthetic QEMU TCG accounting coverage; M156 does not claim an independent throughput gain.
The kernel remains based on the Linux v7.2-rc7 development line and has not completed stable or LTS forward-port requalification.
The build is not independently reproduced on separate physical builders and artifacts are unsigned.
